I wasn’t quite sure where to put this post, but since PuttitOut had Kevdude start a post in PV concerning the recent announcement on Mod Permission Sets the other day, this looks like the best place for this.

It’s been about four days in the Janitor role and I jumped in with both feet and have scrubbed away the advertising spam in v/askvoat, v/whatever, and v/newsubverses; spam from the overnight hit 11, 1, and 1 respectively. The v/askvoat sub is by far the sub with the most spam and v/newsubverses has the least (on a daily basis). Over 200 posts to-date have been deleted in the three subs to make the first few pages of browsing the 'new' submissions look cleaner. From an eyeball glance in the last few days, it appears that spam is slowing in v/whatever and v/newsubverses; v/askvoat is going to need attention for a while before we’ll see any reductions because it had gotten quite bad.

In addition to the posts, I have now deleted about five or six ad-spam comment links and everything of course is available for viewing in the mod logs. I've also made eight new submissions to v/ReportSpammers, a few more would have submitted but they had already been reported, and from the looks of it, I'll be making more posts to that sub going forward. As of the writing of this, I have five more to submit today but have hit the hourly limit (three-per-hour) for submissions. Now for the Admins to find the time to do something about all those reports and throw down some bans.

I've received a few pings to delete posts by what are very probably youtube spammers that appear in v/whatever. I've declined to do anything with these as I have clearly been tasked only to deleting ad-spam by the Admins. Maybe a good plan would be to have an open forum discussion post on what should be done if anything about the youtube and other accounts (posting pics of one sort or another, usu. from imgur) with high SCP | low/zero CCP and whether these constitute any sort of spam threat to Voat that would be worthy of deleting. My take on these is that they be left alone for the votes to sort out: these accounts, while spammy for sure, are not malicious (at the moment anyway), and I think that these sorts of deletions would take time away from the clear ad-spam that needs to go, not even addressing the matter of slippery-deletion-slopes or the inferences that would be required to make these deletion determinations. For my money, these just need to be left alone by L3/Janitors.

Finally, and most importantly, after checking with the co-L2's (@amyacker and @reacher) to make sure that I wasn't needed for a while as I do this Janitor test-gig, I messaged PuttitOut to pull me off the Mod roles in both v/introductions and v/gifs. I could just as easily resign from the mod positions with the click of a button but I want to make it clear to Admins that the limits are important and should not be significantly increased: Access on three defaults at a time (but definitely no more than four if the L3 role is made temporary) is plenty from the perspective of workload and to limit any damage down the road that could be done by a user with visions of some sort of powermod status.

I have suggested elsewhere in this post and on the site that the Janitor role absolutely positively should be temporary - doing this role the right way means not just push-button-deleting spam posts and comments, but includes:

  • Flairing the posts as Spam to let users know this is being addressed and to clearly document the reason in the deletion log,
  • Properly documenting the spam with a mod/distinguished-comment to record the title and username for future use, and
  • For this to be useful in any meaningful way, it requires the extra time to research and report the spammers so that the data can be used by Admins to apply bans or for use in hopefully what will be some coding that will stop the spammers before their posts or comments even hit the site
  • Doing all this on the 13 posts that were deleted today, I have easily spent close to two hours

More posts with updates will follow for Admins’ and Users’ feedback, input, and recommendations on this new Janitor role. And I guarantee that the next updates won’t be quite as long but will always remain thorough.
